reason: Open seafloor fractures provide a plausible path for seawater to enter the circulation loop.
expectation: Seawater will flow down into the fractured rock.

effect: The accumulating early sea has no available combination, so I should try the seawater that has received dissolved minerals instead.
reaction: I was surprised the existing sea could not be used directly.
reason: The mineral-bearing sea may circulate through the open seafloor fractures.
expectation: Seawater will enter the fractured seafloor.

alternatives.reason: Inspection could reveal the correct ingredient if the direct pairing is wrong.

effect: The mineral-bearing seawater enters the crust through the fractures, establishing the first part of the circulation loop.
reaction: The distinction between the two sea items was initially surprising, but the flow now makes sense.
reason: Water entering the crust can encounter hot rock beneath the seafloor.
expectation: The circulating seawater will heat up as it approaches the hot rock.

effect: The seawater is now heated within the crust; it may react with rock before returning to the sea.
reaction: The role of pressure in keeping the hot fluid below the surface is interesting.
reason: The heated water may react further with the hot rock, but its next available step is uncertain.
expectation: Inspection should reveal how the heated water can continue through the circulation loop.

effect: The heated water reacted with buried rock and now carries dissolved material; the next step is likely its return to the sea.
reaction: It is useful to see heating and chemical exchange represented as separate stages.
reason: The hydrothermal fluid must return to the sea, but its available route is not yet clear.
expectation: Inspection should reveal how the fluid rises or mixes with seawater.

effect: The mineral-bearing fluid is rising through fractures toward the seafloor.
reaction: The separate entry and return paths make the circulation loop clearer.
reason: The returning hot fluid can meet the cooler seawater at the vent.
expectation: The hot fluid will emerge into the sea and mix with cooler water.

effect: The returning fluid mixed with cooler seawater, causing minerals to precipitate at the vent.
reaction: The precipitation makes the link between cooling and mineral deposition clear.
reason: The precipitating minerals are the most promising starting point for building the vent deposit, but their next partner is uncertain.
expectation: Inspection will reveal how the precipitated minerals accumulate into a deposit.

effect: Precipitated minerals accumulated around the outlet, completing the deposit goal; the heated-water return goal remains.
reaction: The modest deposit is a useful contrast to assuming every vent forms a chimney.
reason: The returning hot fluid is the clearest starting point for completing the remaining circulation goal.
expectation: Inspection should reveal how the fluid returns to the sea.

effect: The returning fluid formed a hydrothermal plume in the sea, completing the circulation goal and the chapter.
reaction: The distinction between suspended minerals and smoke was a useful final detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the heated water through chemical exchange and back up the fractures made the circulation loop understandable.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first attempt was frustrating: the accumulating sea could not enter the fractures, while the mineral-bearing sea could.

surprise.text: The initially unusable accumulating sea became the partner for the returning fluid at the end.

arbitrary.text: Distinguishing the two sea items as inputs felt somewhat arbitrary, even though both represented seawater.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue for more explanations connecting physical processes to visible results, such as mineral precipitation at the vent.
